endorsements.quote: Healthcare providers and administrators should create clear, concise terms and conditions, as well as educational materials that help patients understand the impact of their data on predictive analytics.
Patients must be the ultimate owners of their data, and infrastructure must be built to both protect patient data and allow patients to readily extricate their information from databases by request.

unlisted_practices: Provide patients clear, concise terms and conditions under one page, written in patient-centered language rather than legal jargon, accessible to all health literacy levels.
Secure patient consent at regular intervals through online portals or in-person reminders at clinic visits.
Adopt privacy-preserving methods such as differential privacy and federated learning in AI data collection and training.
Government and healthcare organizations should invest in creating and enforcing regulatory standards for AI data use to ensure patient safety and trust.
Establish a government-supported third-party regulatory board to develop and enforce transparency and safety standards for AI with ongoing oversight.
Establish patient data ownership, compensation, and reimbursement frameworks for patient data used in AI development.
